rationale: The repository is split feature-first into five milestones ordered by dependency: mathematical/encoding substrate, key objects and key generation/storage, PKCS#1 cryptographic operations, command-line tools, and final public-package integration. This catches defects at the module that owns them: arithmetic and byte conversion bugs before keys depend on them, key serialization bugs before encryption/signing uses keys, PKCS#1 behaviour before CLI wraps it, and import/entry-point wiring last.

milestones.title: Mathematical, byte-transform, PEM, ASN.1, random, and prime foundations
milestones.objective: Implement the pure-Python substrate modules that all higher-level RSA features import: integer sizing and modular arithmetic, raw RSA integer operations, byte/integer transforms, random-number helpers, prime generation, PEM wrapping/parsing, and ASN.1 public-key structures.
milestones.risk_rationale: This milestone delivers the shared low-level contracts used by key generation, serialization, encryption, and signing. Its gate can verify it independently by exercising numeric functions, CRT/inverse behaviour, transform round trips, PEM round trips, ASN.1 class availability, prime predicates, and low-level RSA integer exponentiation without requiring key classes, PKCS#1 padding, or CLI commands. If these contracts are wrong, downstream modules can all appear internally consistent while producing incompatible bytes or mathematically invalid RSA results.

criteria: common.bit_size, byte_size, ceil_div, extended_gcd, inverse, and crt return mathematically correct results for representative positive, zero, and boundary inputs.
common.inverse raises NotRelativePrimeError carrying a, b, and d when no modular inverse exists.
transform converts between bytes and integers without losing leading-zero semantics required by RSA block sizing.
core.encrypt_int and core.decrypt_int perform modular RSA exponentiation and validate integer types and message range.
core.decrypt_int_fast combines per-prime residues with CRT for two-prime and multiprime inputs.
pem saves and loads named PEM blocks with correct base64 wrapping and rejects mismatched or malformed PEM data.
prime and randnum provide usable random integer and prime-generation primitives suitable for later key generation.
asn1 exposes the documented pyasn1 sequence classes for raw and OpenSSL public-key encodings.
corner_cases: bit_size(0) returns 0 and byte_size(0) returns a non-negative valid size.
ceil_div handles exact division and one-over-boundary division.
inverse fails for non-coprime values and succeeds for coprime negative or large inputs where documented.
CRT handles multiple congruences and rejects or fails predictably for invalid modulus relationships.
Integer-to-bytes conversion preserves explicit requested block sizes including leading zero bytes.
RSA integer encryption rejects negative messages, non-integers, and messages greater than or equal to n.
PEM loading tolerates normal line wrapping but rejects wrong marker names and invalid base64.

agents.title: Specification test author
agents.mandate: Write executable tests from the design documents for rsa.common, rsa.core, rsa.transform, rsa.randnum, rsa.prime, rsa.pem, and rsa.asn1, emphasizing independent mathematical and encoding contracts rather than later key APIs.

agents.title: Contract author
agents.mandate: Implement the foundational modules with stable function signatures, exception attributes, byte-layout behaviour, and ASN.1 class exports that later key and PKCS#1 modules will import.

agents.title: Gate repairer
agents.mandate: Repair only the substrate defects named by the acceptance gate, preserving the frozen public symbols and signatures.

milestones.title: RSA key objects, key generation, blinding, and PKCS#1 key storage
milestones.objective: Implement rsa.key and rsa.parallel: AbstractKey, PublicKey, PrivateKey, prime selection, public/private exponent calculation, new key generation including multiprime and poolsize support, blinding helpers, dictionary-like component access, equality/hash/repr, pickling-safe state, and PKCS#1 PEM/DER plus OpenSSL public-key loading/saving.
milestones.risk_rationale: This milestone delivers the key model and serialization contract consumed by PKCS#1 operations and CLI tools. Its gate can verify key generation, component invariants, blinding/unblinding, dictionary-like key access, PEM/DER round trips, OpenSSL public-key parsing, multiprime metadata, and parallel-generation imports without requiring message padding or command-line tools. A defect here would make later encryption/signing either mathematically impossible or byte-incompatible with saved keys.

criteria: PublicKey and PrivateKey expose the documented attributes and support __getitem__, equality, hashing, repr, and pickling-compatible behaviour.
newkeys generates usable public/private key pairs of requested size with default exponent 65537 and custom exponent support.
find_primes and find_p_q generate distinct primes whose product bit length satisfies the accurate parameter contract.
calculate_keys_custom_exponent computes e and d such that RSA round trips work for messages smaller than n.
PrivateKey precomputes CRT data for two-prime and multiprime keys and blinded_decrypt returns the same value as direct private exponentiation.
Public and private keys save and load in PKCS#1 PEM and DER formats.
PublicKey loads OpenSSL PEM and DER public-key structures.
poolsize and parallel generation pathways are available without breaking single-process generation.
corner_cases: Reject or fail predictably when public exponent is not relatively prime to the totient.
Generated p and q are distinct.
accurate=True produces n with the requested bit length.
nprimes greater than 2 records rs, ds, and ts consistently for multiprime decryption.
load_pkcs1 rejects unknown formats and malformed key bytes.
save_pkcs1 rejects unknown formats.
Dictionary-like access rejects unknown component names.
Blinding state updates safely without corrupting decrypt results.

agents.title: Specification test author
agents.mandate: Write executable tests from the design documents for key classes, key generation parameters, blinding, CRT metadata, PEM/DER/OpenSSL serialization, and parallel-generation surface.

agents.title: Implementer
agents.mandate: Implement rsa.key and rsa.parallel using the frozen math, transform, PEM, ASN.1, prime, and core substrate; keep all documented key methods and attributes stable.

agents.title: Contract critic
agents.mandate: Review the implementation for violations of frozen substrate contracts and documented key object signatures, especially serialization byte formats and multiprime CRT fields.

agents.title: Gate repairer
agents.mandate: Fix the reviewer and gate findings in key generation and serialization without changing frozen substrate contracts.

milestones.title: PKCS#1 encryption, decryption, signatures, verification, hashing, and MGF1
milestones.objective: Implement rsa.pkcs1 and rsa.pkcs1_v2 behaviours: PKCS#1 v1.5 encryption/decryption padding, signing and verification padding, file-like signing/verifying, compute_hash and sign_hash workflows, supported hash algorithms, CryptoError hierarchy, and MGF1 for PKCS#1 v2.1 support.
milestones.risk_rationale: This milestone delivers the cryptographic operations that consume frozen key objects. Its gate can verify encrypt/decrypt and sign/verify end-to-end with generated keys, validate PKCS#1 v1.5 padding structure, check supported hash identifiers and ASN.1 prefixes, and test MGF1 determinism without any CLI or package entry-point wiring. If wrong, later CLI and public API can be wired correctly but perform insecure or incompatible cryptography.

criteria: encrypt applies PKCS#1 v1.5 random nonzero padding with at least 8 padding bytes and decrypt reverses it for valid ciphertext.
decrypt raises DecryptionError for malformed blocks, wrong block type, missing separator, ciphertext of wrong size, or messages too long for the key.
sign signs bytes and file-like objects using the requested supported hash method.
verify accepts bytes and file-like objects, returns the hash method name for valid signatures, and raises VerificationError for invalid signatures or mismatched messages.
compute_hash and sign_hash support remote-signing workflows and the documented hash algorithms.
MGF1 returns deterministic masks of requested length using the selected hash algorithm.
CryptoError, DecryptionError, and VerificationError form the documented exception hierarchy.
corner_cases: Encrypting a message longer than key_bytes - 11 fails.
Encryption padding never contains zero bytes before the separator.
Decrypting tampered ciphertext does not leak partial plaintext.
Verification rejects a valid signature over a different message.
Unsupported hash names fail predictably.
Empty messages can be signed and verified.
File-like objects are read as bytes and not confused with path strings.
MGF1 handles zero-length masks and masks longer than one hash digest.

agents.title: Specification test author
agents.mandate: Write executable tests from the design documents for PKCS#1 v1.5 encryption/decryption, signing/verification, hash handling, error classes, file-like inputs, and pkcs1_v2 MGF1.

agents.title: Implementer
agents.mandate: Implement rsa.pkcs1 and rsa.pkcs1_v2 against the frozen key, core, common, and transform contracts, preserving documented exceptions and hash constants.

agents.title: Gate repairer
agents.mandate: Repair only the PKCS#1 and MGF1 behavioural failures named by the gate without altering frozen key or substrate contracts.

milestones.title: Command-line RSA tools
milestones.objective: Implement rsa.cli command utilities and operation classes for pyrsa-keygen, pyrsa-encrypt, pyrsa-decrypt, pyrsa-sign, pyrsa-verify, and pyrsa-priv2pub using optparse and the frozen library behaviours.
milestones.risk_rationale: This milestone delivers the outward-facing command-line feature group that wraps already frozen key and PKCS#1 modules. Its gate can verify argument parsing, stdin/stdout and file I/O handling, key format options, operation class behaviour, generated key files, encryption/decryption command flow, signing/verifying command flow, and verify exit status using direct function invocation or subprocesses. It does not need final package re-export cleanup beyond importing rsa.cli.

criteria: keygen parses the documented options and writes private and optional public keys in PEM or DER format.
CryptoOperation implements common parsing, key loading, input reading, output writing, and call workflow for cryptographic subcommands.
EncryptOperation encrypts bytes with a public key and DecryptOperation decrypts bytes with a private key.
SignOperation signs input bytes with the requested hash method.
VerifyOperation verifies a signature file, produces no output on success, and exits with nonzero status on verification failure.
priv2pub extracts a public key from a private key with independent input and output formats.
Commands support stdin/stdout when input or output filenames are omitted.
corner_cases: Missing required positional arguments produce parser errors.
Invalid key format choices fail predictably.
Binary DER data is not corrupted by text-mode I/O.
Verification failure exits with status 1 and does not write a success payload.
Output omitted writes bytes to stdout without unintended text encoding.
Input omitted reads from stdin.
Sign command requires the hash method positional argument.

agents.title: Specification test author
agents.mandate: Write executable tests from the design documents for optparse CLI behaviour, file/stdin/stdout handling, key formats, operation classes, command workflows, and verification exit status.

agents.title: Implementer
agents.mandate: Implement rsa.cli using the frozen key and PKCS#1 APIs, matching the documented command names, options, positional arguments, and binary I/O semantics.

agents.title: Specification auditor
agents.mandate: Audit cli.py against the PRD command usage blocks and architecture design, reporting option mismatches, missing commands, wrong exit behaviour, or text/binary I/O deviations.

agents.title: Gate repairer
agents.mandate: Fix CLI defects named by the auditor and gate while preserving frozen library APIs.

milestones.title: Public package API, packaging metadata, entry points, and full integration
milestones.objective: Wire the complete public library contract at documented import paths, expose top-level rsa APIs, ensure package metadata and console entry points are correct, include py.typed, prune stray files, and validate the full end-to-end library and CLI workflows.
milestones.risk_rationale: This final milestone integrates all completed feature modules into the public contract. Its gate is the full integration check: consumers must be able to import documented symbols from rsa and submodules, generate keys, save/load them, encrypt/decrypt, sign/verify, use multiprime and custom exponent options, run CLI entry points, and pass visible tests. This belongs last because it depends on every earlier module being complete and freezes the repository-facing surface rather than an internal subsystem.

criteria: import rsa exposes the documented public API for newkeys, key classes, encrypt, decrypt, sign, verify, compute_hash, sign_hash, and public exceptions.
Documented usage examples work end to end from the package root.
Submodules listed in the architecture import successfully on Python 3.8+ with only pyasn1 as a runtime dependency.
Console entry points for pyrsa-keygen, pyrsa-encrypt, pyrsa-decrypt, pyrsa-sign, pyrsa-verify, and pyrsa-priv2pub are declared and dispatch to the implemented CLI behaviours.
pyproject uses Poetry as build backend and declares Python and pyasn1 runtime dependency constraints.
rsa/py.typed exists so type-aware consumers see the package as typed.
Visible check_tests and milestone behavioural tests pass at integration level.
The repository contains no extra scratch implementation copies or undocumented duplicate package trees.
corner_cases: Top-level imports work in a clean environment without relying on local test path hacks.
Package-root exceptions are identical to the submodule exception classes.
PEM/DER keys generated through top-level APIs can be consumed by CLI operations and vice versa.
Entry points handle binary stdin/stdout correctly when installed.
Multiprime key generation remains available through rsa.newkeys.
Unsupported hash and malformed ciphertext errors propagate as documented exception types.
No runtime import requires development dependencies such as pytest, mypy, flake8, tox, Sphinx, or coveralls.

agents.title: Specification test author
agents.mandate: Write executable integration tests from the design documents for package-root imports, usage examples, submodule imports, pyproject metadata, console entry points, and library/CLI interoperability.

agents.title: Implementer
agents.mandate: Wire package-root exports, util helpers, py.typed, Poetry metadata, dependency constraints, and console entry points so the completed modules are reachable through the documented public contract.

agents.title: Specification auditor
agents.mandate: Audit the whole repository against the PRD, architecture design, UML diagrams, command usage blocks, and documented examples; report missing public behaviours or mismatched import paths.

agents.title: Contract critic
agents.mandate: Audit final integration against all previously frozen contracts, confirming no substrate, key, PKCS#1, or CLI symbols were moved, narrowed, or made incompatible.

agents.title: Gate repairer
agents.mandate: Apply the auditor findings, remove stray scratch files or duplicate implementations, and leave only the documented package surface while preserving all frozen contracts.
